result.summary:
Two independent, unrelated root causes, both confirmed by reading the actual source (no literal Windows repro was possible in this Linux sandbox -- see note at end).

SYMPTOM 1 -- wasmex .so-vs-.dll assertion (test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs, describe block 'AC7: the wasmex NIF is a loaded shared library, not an external process', lines 180-198):

Root cause: the two tests in this describe block assert a Unix-specific artifact SHAPE instead of asserting the property AC7 actually cares about (the NIF is compiled-in and bundled, not fetched/spawned at runtime).
  - Line 189: `assert Enum.any?(external_resources, &String.contains?(&1, "native/wasmex/src/"))` assumes Wasmex.Native's :external_resource attributes name paths under a literal `native/wasmex/src/` layout. This directory-shape assumption happens to hold on the Unix build layout this test was written against, but nothing about AC7's actual requirement (no external runtime process) constrains the source-tree layout wasmex's precompiled_nif/rustler build produces its external_resource paths from. This is a fragile coupling to a build-tool implementation detail, not a real cross-platform invariant, and is a plausible source of breakage independent of OS (it would also break if a future wasmex version restructured its own Rust source tree).
  - Line 197: `so_path = Path.join(priv_dir, "native/wasmex.so")` followed by `File.exists?(so_path)` hardcodes the POSIX `.so` shared-library extension and a fixed `native/wasmex.so` relative path. wasmex ships as a `rustler_precompiled` NIF -- the actual bundled filename varies by platform AND is versioned/target-qualified, e.g. `wasmex-v0.15.1-nif-2.15-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.dll` on Windows, `libwasmex-v0.15.1-nif-2.15-x86_64-apple-darwin.so`-style or similar naming on macOS, and a Linux-specific name under priv/native on this sandbox -- never literally `native/wasmex.so`. This assertion was written against whatever the author's own Unix host happened to produce and hardcodes both the extension (`.so` vs `.dll` vs `.dylib`) and the filename (unversioned `wasmex.so` vs the real versioned/target-qualified name). It fails outright on Windows and is not guaranteed to match even on the Linux host actually running this sandbox's suite -- it is coupled to an assumed exact filename that the test never derives from the running system.

What a fix needs to change (not to be implemented by ISSUE-FIXER): both assertions need to test the AC7 property -- 'the NIF is a real loaded/compiled artifact bundled in wasmex's own priv/, not an external process' -- without hardcoding a filename or extension. Concretely: (a) for the .so check, list files under `Path.join(priv_dir, "native")` (or wherever wasmex's actual priv layout puts them -- confirm by inspecting the installed dep in _build/test/lib/wasmex/priv at design time) and assert at least one entry matches a platform-appropriate compiled-library extension for :os.type() (`.so` on unix-linux/freebsd, `.dylib` on unix-darlin i.e. macos matched via :os.type() == {:unix, :darwin}, `.dll` on {:win32, _}), rather than asserting a single literal path exists. (b) for the external_resource check, either loosen the match to something structurally guaranteed by wasmex's own build regardless of internal directory naming (e.g. assert external_resources is non-empty and every entry has a source-code extension appropriate to the NIF language, e.g. ends in ".rs"), or drop the specific 'native/wasmex/src/' substring match in favor of asserting the list is non-empty, since AC7's real claim is 'this module has real external_resource-tracked native build inputs' not 'those inputs live at this literal path'. The fix must derive its expectation from the platform/from wasmex's actual introspectable state at test-run time, not merely wrap the existing Unix-only assertion in `if match?({:unix, _}, :os.type())` -- that would just skip the check on Windows rather than make it correct there, which is explicitly out of scope per the task instructions.

SYMPTOM 2 -- MIX_OS_CONCURRENCY_LOCK / build-directory hard-link contention (scripts/test_parallel.sh):

Root cause: scripts/test_parallel.sh never gives each of the N parallel partitions its own build directory. Step 1 (lines 96-104) does a single `MIX_ENV=test mix compile` up front specifically so the N partitions don't race compiling the same _build/test artifacts concurrently -- but Step 2 (lines 176-204) then launches all N `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=<i> mix test --partitions N ...` processes with no MIX_BUILD_PATH (or any other build-directory) override, so all N processes still share exactly one `_build/test` tree for the whole run, not just for the pre-compile step. Each `mix test` invocation independently re-validates/touches the build manifest and its own lock/consolidation artifacts inside that shared _build/test directory as part of normal Mix startup (compile-manifest check, protocol consolidation cache, `.mix_lock`-style concurrency guard Mix uses internally to serialize access to a given build path from multiple OS processes) even when nothing actually needs recompiling. With N processes pointed at the identical build path simultaneously, this is a real race on the shared path -- it is latent on any OS, but only surfaces as an outright abort on this Windows host because NTFS hard-link creation has stricter semantics/permission requirements than POSIX link(2): a second process's attempt to create a hard link at a path another process is concurrently creating/holding can return ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED on Windows where POSIX filesystems more often tolerate or gracefully serialize the equivalent operation (Mix's own retry/EEXIST handling was seemingly written and tested against POSIX link() failure modes). The '(Mix) could not create hard link ... permission denied' text partitions 4 and 7 aborted with, before either partition ever reached a Result: line, is consistent with exactly this: two of N concurrent `mix test` processes hitting the same shared _build/test path's lock/manifest file at once.

What a fix needs to change: give each partition its own isolated build path, e.g. export `MIX_BUILD_PATH="_build/test-partition-$i"` (or use `mix test --partitions N` in combination with a per-partition `MIX_BUILD_PATH` set right before each backgrounded launch in the Step 2 loop, lines 198-204) so no two concurrently-running `mix test` OS processes ever touch the same on-disk build directory at all -- eliminating the race at its source rather than special-casing Windows' stricter hard-link error surface. This does mean Step 1's single shared pre-compile (which populates the default _build/test) does not by itself warm each partition's now-distinct build path; the fix design needs to decide whether to pre-compile once per target build path, or copy/hardlink the warmed _build/test tree into each partition's build path before backgrounding it, or accept a slower first-partition compile per path -- CODE-DESIGNER should pick based on req113-parallel-test-runner.md's existing AC4/AC5 constraints (lib/letflow/design/req113-parallel-test-runner.md) so as not to reintroduce the exact race Step 1 was written to avoid. A fix that merely detects Windows and serializes/retries hard-link errors would suppress the symptom without removing the shared-path race that causes it, so is out of scope per the task instructions.

Note on repro limits: this sandbox is Linux, so neither symptom could be triggered end-to-end here (no Windows host to build a .dll on, no NTFS to reproduce the hard-link permission-denied error against). Both root causes above were established by reading the actual assertion code and script logic and identifying the specific hardcoded, platform-shape-dependent assumption each makes, not by inferring from the bug report's prose alone -- this is source-level analysis of a confirmed hardcoded literal (the exact `native/wasmex/src/` substring and `native/wasmex.so` path in the test file; the exact absence of any MIX_BUILD_PATH override in the script), which is sound independent of which OS executes it.
